_readme: THE LIVE TO-DO LIST, AS DATA. This file is the source. to-do.md's ranked table is
GENERATED from it by `npm run to-do`, and the Handbook's ranking control reads it.
Edit here — an edit to that table is overwritten.
A list saved from the control comes back with `npm run to-do -- <file>`. It is
validated against the five fields first, and an item Mike settles is NOT removed
until its closure is written on to-do-done-and-parked.md — the command applies
nothing at all until then. An item gone from both pages is an item nobody knows
existed.
FORMATTING IS THE SCRIPT'S. Applying a saved list rewrites this file with two-space
JSON, so do not hand-tune the layout; it will not survive.
Every item must carry all five fields the list's own rules demand — score, why,
risk, askedBy, touches — and tests/unit/toDoItems.test.js fails the build if one
is missing. That guard is the whole reason this file exists: an item missing a
field is a note, and notes are what produced two pieces of unrequested work on
EVERY FIELD HAS A WORD CAP, and tests/unit/toDoItems.test.js fails the build past it:
name 16, why 40, risk 80, touches 80, note 120, comment 120, askedBy.detail 80. A
session with more to say than that puts it in the feature's Brief or history file
and links it. ONE FACT, ONE HOME: replace a sentence that is out of date; never append
an UPDATED paragraph beneath it. On 2026-09-03 one item's comment had grown to 1,388
words across seven sessions that way, and Mike could not read his own list.
activeOn: { machine, since } says which computer is working an item right now —
'laptop' or 'desktop', from the date given. Mike's instruction, 2026-09-03, after item
4.54 was built on both machines in the same week. Absent means nobody is on it. The
page shows it as a column, the control shows it on the row, and the control's save
carries it through. Shutdown clears or keeps it; startup reports the other machine's.
rankedByMike: false marks an item filed after orderedByMikeOn that Mike has not yet
placed. The page and the Handbook control show it. It clears itself: the control's
export does not carry the field, so his next saved list drops it.
ORDER IS MIKE'S RANKING. The array order is the order on screen. It is not
computed from the score, and it must never be re-sorted by a script or a session.
Where his order and the score disagree, his order wins and the score stays
visible so the disagreement is on the page.
KIND — 'defect' or 'feature', and it is a GATE, not a label. A defect is something
that already exists being wrong, missing, unverified or unmaintainable. A feature is a
new capability, page, screen or behaviour. tests/unit/toDoItems.test.js FAILS THE BUILD
on a feature whose askedBy.ours is true — a new thing nobody outside asked for cannot be
filed at all. A defect we found ourselves still can, because Mike never asked us to stop
reporting bugs; he asked us to stop inventing work.
SCORE — 5 security/privacy/data integrity · 4 the user is worse off · 3 helps
sell the package · 2 robustness · 1 internal only · 0 is not filed, it is
deleted with its code.
askedBy.ours = true means NOBODY OUTSIDE ASKED. It is not a defect to record it;
it is a defect to hide it. An item that cannot name Mike or a named outsider has
to justify itself.

items.name: Depreciation rates per country - a manager uploads the source, the AI proposes, they approve
items.why: Depreciation rates and first-year rules differ by country and nothing in the app holds them. The shipped defaults are a guess: Vehicles is 20% where NZ IRD gives 50% diminishing value for a passenger vehicle.
items.risk: An advisor who leaves a default produces a forecast whose depreciation, tax and closing cash are all wrong, and which balances perfectly, and it reaches a lender. The counter-risk is the AI misreading a rate nobody re-checks - which is why the manager approves the extracted table before anything reads it, and why every figure carries its source document and date.

askedBy.detail: 2026-09-08 - 'is it worth having a field in the firm manager hub where tax pdfs can be loaded to be read by the AI so it can be accurate per country?' Filed on his yes, after he overturned the recommendation against it: the uploader is an accountant who should be encouraged to check their sources.

items.touches: A new Firm Manager Hub tab and its upload route, the untrusted-file validation procedure in the master-export-upload skill (last-known-good, version history), an OpenAI extraction route on the Restify backend, an approval gate carrying isApproved, and the six ASSET_SPECS defaults in components/ThreeWayForecastIntake.vue that it would replace.
items.note: NOTHING READS AN UNAPPROVED TABLE, structurally rather than by a flag: a proposal lives in its own store. THE MANAGER'S SIDE IS COMPLETE, slices 1 to 3b. SLICES 4 AND 5 ARE THE ADVISOR'S HALF: each rate badges its origin; an approved table is OFFERED, filling only rates still on defaults so a typed rate survives; and an advisor may LOAD a document while approval stays manager-only. ⚠ THE AI-CALL EXPOSURE THAT WIDENING CREATED IS ITEM 4.82, not a warning here. NOT BUILT: the dated purchase list with the first-year deduction - item 4.77, closed here. No document has been read in earnest; that needs UAT. Detail is in the Brief; rulings in depreciation-rates-history.md.

The recommendation was AGAINST it and he overturned it; the concern that survived was not who uploads but who checks the extraction, which the approve-before-use gate answers. 2026-09-09 - the manager's side built, slices 1 to 3b, after Mike caught the build conflating a tax rate with a depreciation rate and the feature was renamed. Spec Kit produced eleven rulings, Investment Boost among them. Slices 4 and 5 built the same day on his yes: the advisor sees where each rate came from, is offered their country's table, and may load a document their manager decides on. 44 new tests.

items.name: The forecast's tax rates are New Zealand's, hardcoded, for every country
items.why: The forecast applies New Zealand's company tax rate, GST rate and filing cycle to every client in every country, with nothing on screen saying so and no manager able to change it.
items.risk: Every forecast for an overseas client is wrong on tax whether or not it owns a single asset, so this is WIDER than 4.78. An advisor can type over the two rates but is never told they are New Zealand's; the filing cycle they cannot change at all, and it decides which months the money leaves the bank. The statements balance perfectly, which is how it reaches a lender.

askedBy.detail: 2026-09-08 - 'is it worth having a field in the firm manager hub where tax pdfs can be loaded to be read by the AI so it can be accurate per country?' The same request 4.78 was filed under.

items.note: BUILT, SLICES 1-5, AND A SEPARATE TAB FROM DEPRECIATION RATES ON MIKE'S APPROVAL: the country table, the cascade, the routes, the manager's screen, the engine and the advisor's side. FOUR FIGURES, NOT TWO - the drawing found the GST section also fixes the filing cycle and the accounting basis, both New Zealand's. THE ENGINE'S THREE HARDCODED CYCLES BECAME ONE FORMULA, so Australia's quarterly BAS can be expressed at all; the 3,385 golden workbook cells pass unchanged. NOT BUILT: loading a tax PDF for the AI to read, drawn in §4 - today a manager types each figure and its source by hand. Company tax stays ONE flat rate with a free-text line naming which entities it reaches.

Drawing approved the same day, then built in five slices on the laptop. The item's own wording was corrected in the build: both rates WERE already editable by an advisor, so the fault was never 'nothing can change them' but 'they are silently New Zealand's and no manager can set them'. The country field was built here on his explicit yes - it is 4.78's approved addendum and nothing here resolves without it.

items.name: Compliance pages in the four manager hubs
items.why: Mike asked for compliance material that cascades from the mentor down to every firm, and for a firm to declare it understands its own country's law before Meeting Review becomes active.
items.risk: A firm can record a client meeting today with nothing showing it was ever told its obligations. The assessment found two live gaps: IPP3A, in force since 1 May 2026 and unanswerable by software, and IPP12, unevidenced until OpenAI confirms where audio is processed. Without the gate the all-care basis is asserted in a document nobody has to open.

askedBy.detail: 2026-09-10 - 'i want these compliance pages to show in the mentor, global manager, group manager and firm manager hubs - again, cascading'. The gate is his too: 'they have to tick a box before the feature becomes active'.

items.touches: A Compliance tab at all four tiers in TAB_TIERS and NAV_GROUPS, the firmOverlay cascade, an upload route reusing the master-export-upload validation, an on-demand AI completeness check against MEETING-REVIEW-DPIA.md section 9, the declaration record, and a locked state on pages/meeting-record.vue.
items.note: ALL FOUR SLICES BUILT: the cascade read-only downward, the evidence pack, the declaration and its GATE, the check and the roll-up. THE GATE IS PER FIRM: one that has ticked records as before, one that has not cannot start, and neither affects the other. NO FIRM HAS TICKED YET, so each needs its manager to do it once. THE DECLARATION IS MIKE'S OWN WORDS, VERBATIM AND PINNED. The declaration GATES, the check NEVER does - three tests fail if anything else starts gating. THE CHECK IS SENT DOCUMENT NAMES, NEVER CONTENTS. A tier may neither edit nor hide what a tier above published - structural, not a check. UNSEEN: needs MySQL, Drive and a model key. Brief: design/features/compliance.md.

items.name: Learning from outcomes across consenting firms - the platform gets smarter with use
items.why: Case reviews already record how each template landed, and the engine reads that back for the same client only. Pooled across firms that consent, anonymised, it can adjust recommendations for everyone.
items.risk: Without it the product cannot honestly claim to get smarter with use beyond one client. The counter-risk is privacy: identifiers or client words leaving a firm, or a firm that never consented being changed by others' outcomes - both refused by the spec.

askedBy.detail: 2026-09-10 - 'build a prompt to develop the task to enable real machine learning - such that it does, indeed, get smarter with use. Not just from one firm, but from all those who consent to help develop the model by sharing anonymised data'.

items.touches: caseStore.js template_outcomes and the mentor-share anonymiser, priorEngagement.js, the distinction-boost seam in templateResolver.js, the decision trace, a firm-tier consent tab and a Mentor Hub page in FirmManagerHub.vue, the overlay store at platform scope, the Scenario Lab.
items.note: SPEC KIT FEATURE, specs/002-outcome-learning. Explainable code, not a black-box model: pooled verdicts become capped score adjustments through the same seam as distinction boosts, published only above a firm-and-case floor and only after the mentor accepts each one; every applied adjustment shows on the decision trace with its evidence. Nothing leaves a firm that has not opted in. Three drawings come before any code.

items.name: A refused document cannot tell a manager why
items.why: A manager told a document could not be read is advised to download it again or try another edition. The model's own reason is now captured server-side and never reaches them.
items.risk: The section 3 fix removed the worst case - a legible document that disagrees with itself is no longer refused - so the standing advice is sound in the common case. What remains is a manager who cannot act on a refusal and re-loads the same file, paying for each attempt. That is what happened three times on 2026-09-11.

items.note: THE MATERIAL NOW EXISTS: the model is asked for one plain sentence saying what defeated it, and it is logged. Whether any of it reaches a manager is a WORDING DECISION FOR MIKE, since UNREADABLE_MESSAGE is his own pinned sentence and a test fails the build if it drifts.

items.name: Only 250 of about 2,800 published classes are kept
items.why: MAX_CLASSES is 250 and IR265 publishes roughly 2,800 classes. A manager's picker would hold the first tenth of the document and stop, with nothing on screen saying so.
items.risk: A manager whose category matched the wrong class looks for the right one in a picker that ends around page 10 of 52, does not find it, and has no way to know the class is in the document. Dropped classes are deliberately not counted into refusedRows, so the absence is silent by design.

askedBy.detail: Found 2026-09-11 while building the section 3 fix, and filed on Mike's yes. A defect in something already built, not a new capability.

What REMAINS is narrow - the per-document cap is still 250 and its code comment still says 'about 156', which bites only a firm whose group has loaded no country schedule. The Brief's copy of the wrong figure was corrected 2026-09-11. FOR MIKE: close it, or fix the comment and the cap first.

items.name: A read can succeed and propose no rates at all
items.why: IR265 was read, named and dated correctly, and three real contradictions in it were flagged - then not one rate and not one class was proposed. The manager gets a pending document with nothing on it to approve.
items.risk: A manager loads a schedule, waits, pays for the reading and is shown a proposal that proposes nothing, with no way to tell whether the document was poor or the reading was. Every forecast keeps the app's own six figures, which are New Zealand guesses, and the screen does not say that is why.

askedBy.detail: Found 2026-09-11 by loading the real IR265 after the section 3 fix, and filed on Mike's yes. A defect in something already built.

items.touches: The rates and classlist sections of the depreciation-read prompt in data/ai-prompts.json, validateReading in server/utils/depreciationExtract.js, and whatever the country-wide table Mike asked for on 2026-09-11 does instead.
items.note: PROVEN, NOT INFERRED: refusedRows was 0, so nothing was rejected on our side - the model sent an empty rates list. THE CURE IS BUILT IN 4.92: a schedule is now read a page range at a time and a read producing no classes is refused outright rather than stored as a proposal with nothing on it. That is the country path only. THE PER-DOCUMENT READ IS UNCHANGED and still asks for a whole schedule in one answer. FOR MIKE: close it, or point the per-document read at the same passes.
items.comment: 2026-09-11 - the second wall, met immediately after the first came down. The section 3 fix worked: the document that had been refused four times was read, named IR265, dated 2023-10, and three genuine contradictions surfaced - powder dryer buildings at two rates on pages 14 and 46, microwave ovens twice on page 36, and the Southern Cross Cable entry.

items.name: A country's whole rate schedule, stored as a searchable table
items.blocks: 4.90 and 4.91, which both come back to one reply carrying a 52-page schedule
items.why: Mike asked for a country's published schedule to be stored and turned into a searchable table the models can use, instead of being re-read per firm and reduced to six rough categories.
items.risk: Without it every firm pays to re-read the same document, an advisor's client is depreciated at the nearest of six buckets rather than the class the tax authority publishes, and nothing accumulates. It is also the likely cure for 4.90 and 4.91: a table is built up in sections, so no single answer has to carry 2,800 classes.

askedBy.detail: 2026-09-11 - 'if a single source of truth doc is available for a country - with ALL depreciation rates in it - we need the capability to store it, save it, translate it into a serachable table so it can be used in our models'.

items.touches: A new store beside the approved tables, the reading route and prompt in depreciationExtract.js and data/ai-prompts.json, the tier chain and the global-group scope in tierChain.js, a screen at the global group manager tier in FirmManagerHub.vue, and the class picker in DepreciationDocumentReview.vue.
items.note: 🔴 MIKE'S RULING, 2026-09-11: IT LOADS AT THE GLOBAL GROUP MANAGER TIER. One person loads the schedules for every country their brand operates in, each table tagged with its country; group managers and firms inherit the one matching their client and load nothing. This OVERRIDES the default-is-mentor-alone rule for this feature. PER COUNTRY, NOT PER DOCUMENT: each row names the document and page it came from. BUILT 2026-09-11, ALL FIVE SLICES: the store, the sectioned read, six routes with their own 10-a-day allowance, the global group manager's screen, and the firm's class picker searching the whole table. Drawing: design/mockups/depreciation-rates-country-schedules.html. NO REAL SCHEDULE HAS BEEN READ THROUGH IT - that needs UAT.
